# decoder/ - training and testing the RFD4 decoder

**What the decoder does:** it turns the per-residue "latent" vectors (made by the encoder, or generated by the denoiser) back into atoms and residue names. We fine-tuned it so that it understands 189 residue classes (147 original + 29 NCAAs + 13 D-forms), places the atoms of NCAAs correctly, keeps D-forms mirror-handed and keeps peptide bonds the right length.

| File / folder | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **`decoder_train.py`** | **the one training script** for every run (loss weights are environment variables; the long header explains data, losses and all variables) |
| `bond_loss.py` | the peptide-bond loss and the clash loss used by `decoder_train.py` (upload them together) |
| `PRESETS.md` | **one row per run**: weights file, start point, settings, job, result. Read this to see what each run was |
| `slurm/` | cluster job files; `decoder_train_h200.slurm` is the generic one (run 8 defaults), the others are the originals of each run |
| `logs/` | training logs of runs "run 2" to run 8 (`dec_v*_<job>.log`) |
| `eval/` | scripts that test a decoder on real structures (`eval_one_dec.py`, `eval_one_dec_blind.py`, `eval_real_autoencoder.py`) and their launchers |
| `history/` | the 11 earlier versions of the training script (`decoder_fine_tune.py`, `_v2` to `_v10`); each added one loss term. Kept so old logs can be traced; use `decoder_train.py` instead |

Weights: [`../weights/decoder/`](../weights/decoder/) (see `../weights/README.md`). **Default decoder = run 8** (`decoder_v9_499602.pt`).

## The story in five lines
1. Naming (runs 1 to 3): teach the decoder the new residue classes; real PDB peptides are named 99.6% correctly.
2. The decoder was the cap on D-form handedness (it placed generated D-forms correctly only 35-42% of the time): adding an atom-coordinate loss (run 5/5b) and a chirality loss (runs 6, 7) fixed it (92-100%).
3. A peptide-bond loss (run 8) lifted sensible bonds in generated designs from 67-74% to 83-87%: default decoder.
4. A clash loss (run 9) changed nothing useful.
5. Remaining weakness: about 20% of designs have an atom pair closer than 2 A to the receptor; this comes from side-chain placement that the decoder cannot fix because it never sees the receptor (Results.MD 65).

## Quick example (run 8 recipe on the cluster)
```
sbatch decoder/slurm/decoder_train_h200.slurm
# other runs: sbatch --export=ALL,INIT_DEC=<start .pt>,STRUCT_W=0.25,CHI_W=0,BOND_W=0 decoder/slurm/decoder_train_h200.slurm
```
Output: a `.pt` file with the best epoch's decoder weights, plus a log with per-epoch handedness, bond and clash numbers.
